claims.description: Helped secure the Altan peace and tribute settlement and defended himself against Gao Yongchun’s salt-administration accusations.
Proposed easing harsh administration and excessive levies after an imperial prince was born; the emperor accepted the memorial.
Protected Yunnan officials and prevented withdrawal of stored mining silver before leaving for mourning.
Reformed rites administration, resisted Zhang Guoxiang’s title restoration, and restored limits on Altan’s tribute rewards.
Urged a strong response to Huoluochi’s invasion and defended himself against Ren Rang.
Pressed for investiture of the heir and retired after the emperor rebuked him.
Argued that civil officials were punished unfairly after the Liaodong disaster and repeatedly remonstrated on court policy.
Requested a self-reproach edict, a settled succession, an end to mining taxes, and rites for the eldest imperial son.
Proposed daily court diaries as source material for future Veritable Records; Zhang Juzheng implemented the plan.
Proposed a long-term Chinese military administration in Korea and recommended Yang Hao and Xing Jie.
Was accused of corruptly promoting Yang Hao and stripped of office after the emperor rejected his defense.
Opposed mining taxes, coauthored three policy treatises, and intervened to prevent indiscriminate prosecution in the sorcerous-book case.
Defended the integrity of the official review system and delayed costly palace construction.
Pressed the emperor to complete censorate appointments and died in office after sustained attacks.
